summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and chronic back pain was admitted for recurrent nausea and vomiting. She had tried Zofran at home without success and presented with worsening symptoms and back pain. IV antiemetics provided relief, and she tolerated advancement to a regular diabetic diet. Her blood glucose remained stable except for one episode of mild hypoglycemia, managed with food. The insulin regimen was unchanged. Gabapentin was started for back pain as a required trial before lidocaine patch approval. She was advised to use Ativan instead of Zofran for future nausea episodes. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned with her new care team, including the Chronic Pain Service.
problems: Diabetes with unspecified complication, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
